question.text: Let the point <math><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></math> be the reflection of the point <math><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mn>3</mn></mrow></mfenced></math> with respect to the line <math><mn>8</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>6</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">y</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>23</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo></math> Let <math><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></mrow></msub></math> and <math><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></mrow></msub></math> be circle of radii <math><mn>2</mn></math> and <math><mn>1</mn></math> with centres <math><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math> and <math><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></math> respectively. Let <math><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></math> be a common tangent to the circle <math><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></mrow></msub></math> and <math><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></mrow></msub></math> such that both the circle are on the same side of <math><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi><mo>.</mo></math> If <math><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math> is the point of intersection of <math><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></math> and the line passing through <math><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math> and <math><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mo>,</mo></math> then the length of the line segment <math><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math> is ___________.

solution.text:
Clearly, ACP and BCQ are similar triangles.
Hence,
ACBC=r1r2
ACBC=2
AC=2BC ...(i)

Now, since B , is image of A in line 8x-6y=23
AD=BD
AB=2AD ...(ii)
AD= distance of A from line
8x- 6y=23
AD=16-16-2310=52
Now as AC=2BC
⇒AC=2(AC-AB)
⇒AC=2AB
⇒AC=4AD (from (ii))
AC=4×52
AC=10
